chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, or someone else, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah or Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding

the man who buys the thing which spoils during its day, and he leaves it until he comes with the price. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he comes with the price between it and the night, then [the sale stands], otherwise, there is no sale for him.'

key_terms.بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ اللَّيْلِ: between it (the day) and the night

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling perishable items if payment is delayed until the next day?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the 'khiyar al-shart' (option of stipulation) for perishable goods, establishing a specific timeframe where the seller retains the right to rescind the contract if payment is delayed until nightfall. It highlights the practical application of avoiding *gharar* (uncertainty) in trade by linking the validity of the sale to the immediate availability of funds, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding commercial transactions.
